newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: AMF mulls Kipushi zinc options in new Congo.
newsitem.headline: AMF mulls Kipushi zinc options in new Congo.

text.p: America Mineral Fields Inc said on Friday it was considering various options for smelting zinc from the Kipushi mine in new Congo, including possibly shipping ore to South Africa.
But AMF director Richard Garnett told Reuters his company would most likely go ahead with plans to build its own smelter at the mine.
Garnett said he had met Gencor Ltd to discuss the possibility of supplying ore to a zinc smelter Gencor was considering building in the Eastern Cape of South Africa.
"We have had a meeting with Gencor, which I attended in Johannesburg, and we advised each other of our plans, preliminary as they are at this stage," he said.
"It sounds a nice idea but, without having costed anything out, my gut feel is that it might not be possible," he added, pointing out it was a long way to South Africa's Eastern Cape Province.
"We are proceeding with a full feasibility study of putting in a smelter ourselves at Kipushi."

Should AMF embark on the full Kipushi project -- rehabilitation of the underground mine, processing the tailings and building a 200,000-tonnes-a-year zinc smelter -- total capital expenditure would be between $600 and $700 million, Garnett said.
U.S.-based AMF was awarded the right to the Kipushi zinc project by Laurent Kabila's rebel alliance in control of the area in April.
Former Zaire's Kipushi zinc mine is situated just outside the country's second city Lubumbashi in the mineral-rich, southern province of Katanga.
The underground zinc mine was closed in 1993 due to lack of funding from the former government.
AMF, the first international company to be awarded a project by the new government, plans to revamp and develop Kipushi as part of a joint venture with the state mining company Gecamines.
"Kipushi mine really ranks as one of the world's major zinc mines. It has in situ reserves, proven and probable, worth around $4.5 billion," Garnett said earlier.
Garnett said that building an on-site smelter would encourage further zinc exploration in the area.
"Once you have a smelter in place, it's amazing but then everyone starts looking for that commodity and it will encourage more exploration," he said.

Asked if AMF would consider exploring and developing that part of the ore body that extends into Zambia, Garnett said the company was interested but it would be 15 to 20 years before anything happened on that front.
